texts.li: [their:freedbyA] {X_nameDef} won't hand the bundle to just anyone. It is for {A_nameDef}, by name, from {FACTION} at {PLACE}. The colony {TALE}, and when {FACTION} tell that story it's {A_nameDef}'s face they picture.\n\nThe bundle holds goods worth about {COUNT} silver, sent to settle the debt.

[their:tendedbyA] Before {X_nameDef} would even set the pack down, there was one question: is {A_nameDef} here? The colony {TALE}, and {FACTION} remember whose hands did the stitching.\n\n{X_nameDef} has carried a gift worth about {COUNT} silver from {PLACE}, and wants to pay it to the right person.

[theirLowtech] The speech was rehearsed the whole way from {PLACE}, and {X_nameDef} gets through every word of it before setting down the heavy pack. {FACTION} have not forgotten that the colony {TALE}, and their elders sent {X_nameDef} to settle the debt.\n\nThe pack holds goods worth about {COUNT} silver. {X_nameDef} has been told not to carry it home again.

[theirHightech] {FACTION} keep accounts, and one of them has stood open since the colony {TALE}. {X_nameDef} has come from {PLACE} to close it, with a crate of goods worth about {COUNT} silver and a receipt for someone to sign.

[deed:released,named] A family at {PLACE} has been putting things by since the colony {TALE}. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has carried their gift up the road, worth about {COUNT} silver, along with their thanks and a list of every one of them who wanted to be named.
[deed:tended] The colony {TALE}. {FACTION} were in no state to pay for it then. They are now.\n\n{X_nameDef} has brought the payment up from {PLACE}, in goods worth about {COUNT} silver.
[deed:hardship] {PLACE} has had its first good year in five. {FACTION} haven't forgotten that the colony {TALE}, and {X_nameDef} has walked up to say so, with a gift worth about {COUNT} silver.

[longago] {A_nameDef} had to be reminded. It was a long time ago that the colony {TALE}, and most here had let it go. {FACTION} had not.\n\nTheir envoy, {X_nameDef}, has come from {PLACE} with a gift worth about {COUNT} silver to settle the matter at last.

{FACTION} don't like owing anyone, {X_nameDef} tells {A_nameDef}, and they have owed the colony since it {TALE}. {X_nameDef} has brought a gift worth about {COUNT} silver up from {PLACE} to put that right.

li.label: Accept the gift
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} sets the gift down and says the words {FACTION} use to close a debt. Then {X_nameDef} asks for a cup of water before the long walk home.

outcomes.li: [theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} lays the gift out on a blanket, names each thing in turn, and declares the debt paid.
[theirHightech] {X_nameDef} has {A_nameDef} sign for the crate, in two places, and declares the account closed.

li.label: Accept it, and feast their envoy (20 raw food)
li.outcome: The gift goes into the stores and {X_nameDef} goes to the head of the table. By the second bowl {X_nameDef} is telling the colony how the story of what it did is told at {PLACE}, with parts in it the colony doesn't remember at all. {X_nameDef} leaves in the morning with good things to say at {PLACE}.

outcomes.li: [winter] The gift goes into the stores and {X_nameDef} gets the seat nearest the hearth. The talk runs late, and {X_nameDef} leaves in the morning with good things to say at {PLACE}.
[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} sees to {X_nameDef}'s place at the table personally, and to {X_possessive} second helping. {X_nameDef} leaves in the morning with good things to say at {PLACE}.

li.label: Tell them they owe nothing
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} tells {X_nameDef} the colony did what anyone should have, and won't be paid for it. {X_nameDef} says the words back slowly, to be sure of carrying them home right, and shoulders the gift again.

outcomes.li: [colony:Generous] {A_nameDef} tells {X_nameDef} the colony doesn't keep accounts with its neighbors. {X_nameDef} takes the gift home, along with a story {FACTION} will tell for years.

li.label: Ask for something the colony needs instead (a good talker)
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} sat down with {X_nameDef} and went through the gift piece by piece, trading the fine things the colony has no use for against plain things it does. By the end {X_nameDef} was making suggestions of {X_possessive} own.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} pushed too hard. {X_nameDef} left the gift as it was, called the debt settled in a few cold words, and set off for {PLACE} early.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has come from {PLACE} with a request, and is too polite to remind anyone why the colony should listen. {A_nameDef} remembers anyway that {FACTION} {TALE}.\n\nA bad season has left {PLACE} short of nearly everything. {FACTION} would be grateful for {COUNT} silver, or whatever help the colony can give.

[deed:aid] {FACTION} sent their fighters when the colony called, and never sent a bill. {X_nameDef} has come from {PLACE} with one now, politely. The town's walls need work, and {FACTION} ask {COUNT} silver toward them, or whatever else the colony can do.

[deed:relief] The granary at {PLACE} burned to the ground ten days ago, with most of the winter's grain inside. Not long ago {FACTION} {TALE}, and now {X_nameDef} has come to ask the same of the colony: {COUNT} silver, or any help it can spare.

[deed:taught] The well at {PLACE} has gone bad, and {X_nameDef} has come to ask for help with a new one: {COUNT} silver, or whatever the colony can put toward it. {FACTION} {TALE}, as {X_nameDef} is careful to mention, and never charged for the lessons.

[deed:granted] The letter {X_nameDef} carried from {PLACE} is short, and sealed in {FACTION}'s wax. It reminds the colony that {FACTION} {TALE}. It notes that the year's levy has come in light. It asks for {COUNT} silver, or such other help as the colony sees fit to give, and it does not say please.

[winter] {X_nameDef} came up the frozen road from {PLACE} with a list of everything the town has run out of, and it is a long list. {FACTION} {TALE}, and they've come to call in the favor: {COUNT} silver to see {PLACE} through the cold, or what help the colony can manage.

[theirHightech] The request {X_nameDef} carries from {PLACE} is typed, numbered and signed by three people of {FACTION}.

Item one: {FACTION} {TALE}.
Item two: a storm has taken the roof off the pump house.
Item three: {COUNT} silver, or assistance in kind.

li.label: Send {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} ties the purse inside {X_possessive} coat and sets off for {PLACE} before dark. Between the colony and {FACTION}, the account is square.

li.label: Send medicine instead (8)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} packs the medicine in straw for the road. The healers at {PLACE} will be gladder of it than of silver, {X_pronoun} says, and the favor is returned.

li.label: Draw up plans for their rebuilding (a builder)
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} spent the evening bent over the table, {X_nameDef} describing {PLACE} from memory and {B_nameDef} drawing it better. {X_nameDef} rolled the plans up as carefully as if they were money, and said {FACTION} could not have asked for more.

outcomes.li: [b:trait:TooSmart] {B_nameDef} redraws the plans for {PLACE} three times, each better than the last, and explains all three. {X_nameDef} takes the last one home, and the favor is returned.

li.reason: Nobody here builds well enough to draw up plans for a town.

li.label: The colony can't help this time
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} says {FACTION} will understand, and starts back down the road within the hour. They won't forget that they asked.

texts.li: [food,their:friend] Word got to {PLACE} that {FRIEND_nameDef} might be going hungry, and for {FACTION} that was enough. The colony {TALE}, and they have sent {X_nameDef} up the road with {COUNT} {THING}.\n\n{X_nameDef} won't hear of a price.

[medicine,their:friend] {X_nameDef}'s first question is for {FRIEND_nameDef}: are you well? The second is where to put the medicine. The colony {TALE}, and {FACTION} have sent {COUNT} {THING} from {PLACE}, no payment wanted.

[food] {COUNT} {THING} have come up the road from {PLACE}, carried by {X_nameDef} and the others {FACTION} sent along. Word reached them that times are hard here, and they remember that the colony {TALE}.\n\n{X_nameDef} says there's no price, and won't hear of one.

[medicine,sick] {FACTION} heard that people here were sick. They didn't send a letter. They sent {X_nameDef}, from {PLACE}, with {COUNT} {THING}, because they remember that the colony {TALE}, and {X_nameDef} won't take a coin for it.

[medicine,plague] With the plague moving through the region, every healer is counting doses. {FACTION} counted theirs and found {COUNT} {THING} to spare for the colony, which once {TALE}. {X_nameDef} has brought it from {PLACE}, and won't take silver for it.

[food,famine] Half the region is going hungry this year, {PLACE} with it. {FACTION} have sent {X_nameDef} up the road anyway, with {COUNT} {THING} they can barely spare, for the colony that once {TALE}.\n\n{X_nameDef} won't take silver for it.

[food,winter] The road from {PLACE} is half snowed in, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} came up it anyway, dragging a sled of {COUNT} {THING}. {FACTION} remember that the colony {TALE}. They thought it might be a hard winter here too.

[food,hungry] Someone at {PLACE} heard the colony's stores were running low. {FACTION} remember that the colony {TALE}, and {X_nameDef} has come with {COUNT} {THING}. It's a gift, {X_nameDef} says, and that's the end of it.

[deed:released,named] The colony {TALE}, and a family at {PLACE} has been waiting for a way to repay it ever since. Hard times here are their chance. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has brought {COUNT} {THING}, with the family's love.
[deed:hardship] When {PLACE} had its hard year, the colony stood by it. This is the colony's hard year. {FACTION} have sent {X_nameDef} with {COUNT} {THING}.

li.label: Accept it with thanks
li.outcome: The {THING} is stacked inside the gate, and the colony pours {X_nameDef}'s people a drink before they turn for {PLACE}. Now it's the colony that owes {FACTION}.

outcomes.li: [winter] The {THING} is carried in out of the snow, and {X_nameDef}'s people warm their hands at the colony's hearth before turning back to {PLACE}. Now the colony owes {FACTION} one.
[trait:Greedy] {A_nameDef} counts the {THING} before saying thank you, then counts it again. {X_nameDef} lets that pass, and heads home to {PLACE}.

li.label: Accept it, and send them home with silver (60)
li.outcome: The colony takes the {THING} and tries to press a purse into {X_nameDef}'s hands for the road. {X_nameDef} pushes it back twice. The third time, {X_nameDef} keeps it.

li.label: Feed their carters before the road home (a cook, 15 raw food)
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} cooks for the people from {PLACE}, and they eat like people who've been on the road since dawn, which they have. They leave the {THING}, and a good word for the colony.

li.label: Thank them, and ask them to give it to someone worse off
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} knows a village two days on that is worse off than the colony. The load goes there instead, and {FACTION} will hear whose idea it was.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} waits beyond the fields with both hands open and held away from {X_possessive} sides. The envoy is old, and so is the feud between {FACTION} and the colony. Half the young people at home, {X_nameDef} says, couldn't tell you what it was about.\n\n{FACTION} offer peace, and ask nothing for it.

[ourwrong] Alone and on foot, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come as far as the edge of the colony's land, and no further. {FACTION} have not forgotten that the colony {TALE}, {X_nameDef} says, and they don't ask the colony to forget what they did either. But the young ones who swore the feud are going gray now.\n\n{FACTION} offer peace, and ask nothing for it.

[theirwrong] {FACTION} {TALE}. {X_nameDef} says so first, before anything else, standing at the edge of the colony's land, with no excuses and no talk of what the colony did back. {FACTION} want it ended.\n\nThey offer peace, freely.

[killedours] {DEAD}. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} knows that name; among {FACTION}, everyone does. The envoy waits outside the colony under a white cloth, and says {FACTION} want the feud to end with this generation, and not pass to the next.\n\n{FACTION} offer peace. {A_nameDef} thinks the colony could ask for more than words.

[tribal] A pipe-bearer of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has sat down in the grass beyond the fields with a carved pipe across {X_possessive} knees. The pipe is unlit. There has been no blood between {FACTION} and the colony for many moons, and {FACTION} would like to light it together.\n\nThey ask nothing for peace.

[theirHightech] "The present council of {FACTION} regards the old hostilities as closed." {X_nameDef}, their negotiator, reads it off a card at the edge of the colony's land, unarmed, then puts the card away. "They want peace," {X_nameDef} says. "No conditions. I'd take it."

li.label: Make peace
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} walks out to the edge of the fields and takes {X_nameDef}'s hand. Neither of them says much. {FACTION} will have the news by nightfall.

outcomes.li: [tribal] The pipe is lit at last, and passed between {X_nameDef} and {A_nameDef} until the bowl is ash. {X_nameDef} carries the cold pipe home to {FACTION} to show them.
[trait:Bloodlust] {A_nameDef} takes {X_nameDef}'s hand as if it might bite. The peace is made all the same, and {X_nameDef} is gone toward {FACTION} before anyone can think better of it.

li.label: Make peace, and ask weregild for the colony's dead (a good talker)
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} says {DEAD}'s name, then the price, and holds {X_nameDef}'s eye through the silence after. {X_nameDef} agrees. {COUNT} silver will come with the peace.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} says {FACTION} will not pay a blood-price for a feud both sides fed. The envoy goes home, and the feud goes on.

li.label: Make peace over a meal (25 raw food)
li.outcome: The colony carries bread and stew out to where {X_nameDef} waits, and {A_nameDef} sits down in the grass across from {X_objective}. They eat slowly, and talk more as the bowls empty. {X_nameDef} goes home with the peace and a full belly.

li.label: Send the envoy away
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} waits until dusk for a different answer, then walks back the way {X_pronoun} came. The feud goes on.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, an elder of {FACTION}, and an envoy of {ENEMY} have come to the colony together, which shows how far things have gone. The two peoples are quarreling over {TALE}, and neither will take the other's word for anything.\n\n{FACTION} trust the colony, {X_nameDef} says, and {ENEMY} have agreed to accept its judgment.

[grateful] "You tell them," {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} says to the envoy of {ENEMY}. "It's your quarrel."
"It's yours," says the envoy.

It's over {TALE}. {FACTION} remember the colony's help, and have asked it to judge between them; {ENEMY} have agreed to abide by that, with bad grace.

[theirLowtech] Two elders, one of {FACTION} and one of {ENEMY}, have walked to the colony together without a word to each other the whole way. Their peoples have quarreled over {TALE} since the last moon.\n\nThey've agreed on one thing: the colony should judge.

[theirHightech] {X_nameDef}, an administrator of {FACTION}, has arrived with a counterpart from {ENEMY} and two folders of documents about {TALE}. Neither side accepts the other's papers. Both have agreed to accept the colony's word.\n\nThey ask the colony to arbitrate.

[colony:Merciful|colony:Open] The colony's name for fair dealing has reached {FACTION}. {X_nameDef} has come with an envoy of {ENEMY} and a quarrel over {TALE} that has gone on long enough, and they want the colony to settle it.

li.label: Side with {FACTION}
li.outcome: The colony finds for {FACTION}. {X_nameDef} shakes {A_nameDef}'s hand twice over. The envoy of {ENEMY} is on the road before the handshaking is done, and {ENEMY} will remember it.

li.label: Side with {ENEMY}
li.outcome: The colony finds for {ENEMY}. Their envoy can hardly believe it. {X_nameDef} goes home to {PLACE} stiff and silent, and {FACTION} will remember who they trusted.

li.label: Hear both sides and judge fairly (a good talker)
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} hears both sides out until the lamp burns low, asks the same questions twice, and splits it down the middle. Both envoys grumble, and both shake on it.

outcomes.li: [b:trait:Kind] {B_nameDef} lets each envoy talk until there's nothing left to say, then asks each of them what the other wants. By morning they've worked most of it out themselves, and both thank {B_nameDef} for it.

[b:office:Speaker] {B_nameDef}, the colony's speaker, runs it like a council meeting: each side in turn, no interrupting, a vote at the end. The envoys find this so strange that they agree to the judgment.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} hears them out and gives a judgment. Neither side likes it, and both go home saying the colony favored the other.

li.label: It's not the colony's quarrel
li.outcome: The colony won't judge. The two envoys share the road home as far as the first fork, without a word between them.

matters.li: a spring both towns water their herds at
a boundary stone that moved in the night
who may cut timber in the old wood between them
a herd of goats that wandered across the line and never came back
a debt from a bad harvest, three years old
a promise of marriage between two families that one of them broke
a hunting ground both claim from their grandfathers' time
[winter] a stand of firewood both of them claim
[industrial|spacer] a road one of them wants to build through the other's fields
[hills] grazing on the hills between them
who should pay to mend the bridge both of them use
a bull that broke through a fence, and the calves it sired on the other side
